title: Low-Poly 3D Modeling & VR Optimization
description: Across H-0P3 and Bridge Captain, I created low-poly 3D models, hand-painted textures, character rigs, spacecraft, and game-ready environments when the projects required custom assets. For Bridge Captain VR, I designed the entire bridge environment and seven crew members around the performance limits of mobile stereoscopic VR, keeping the complete scene to roughly 10,000 polygons while maintaining 60 FPS on a Galaxy S6 Edge / Gear VR.

sections.title: Learning to Build My Own Assets
paragraphs: I was never primarily a professional artist, but independent game development often meant creating the assets I needed myself. Over the years I worked with MilkShape, 3ds Max, and Blender to create low-poly ships, environments, props, characters, and other production assets.

sections.title: H-0P3 Modeling
paragraphs: H-0P3 was one of my earliest projects where I created my own 3D game assets. I modeled the ships and other visual elements myself and used the project as an opportunity to develop the practical 3D skills needed to support my own game designs.

sections.title: Low-Poly Spacecraft
paragraphs: Across H-0P3 and Bridge Captain, I created a range of low-poly spacecraft using the same performance-first modeling approach. These ships were built in tools such as 3ds Max, MilkShape, and Blender and were designed to fit the visual and performance constraints of the projects they supported.

sections.title: Bridge Captain VR
paragraphs: For the Gear VR generation of Bridge Captain, I modeled the bridge environment, consoles, crew members, and related assets primarily in Blender. I also created most of the textures myself in Photoshop and set up the final scene lighting in Unity.

sections.title: Character Modeling & Rigging
paragraphs: I created all seven crew characters used in the VR bridge and rigged them in Blender. The characters were deliberately stylized and low-poly so they could remain visible inside the bridge without overwhelming the rendering budget.

sections.title: Designed for Mobile VR
paragraphs: The target hardware was a Samsung Galaxy S6 Edge running Gear VR, where the scene needed to render stereoscopically at 60 FPS. Rather than building high-detail assets and trying to optimize them afterward, I authored the bridge and characters around a low-poly visual style from the beginning.

sections.title: 10K-Polygon Complete Bridge
paragraphs: The complete bridge environment plus all seven crew members came to roughly 10,000 polygons in the working VR build. That was already enough to support playable missions while maintaining the target performance.

I had not yet finished adding all of the visual variety I originally wanted, but based on the performance headroom I expected roughly 20,000 polygons would still have provided ample room for the completed scene.

sections.title: Texture & Visual Workflow
paragraphs: Most of the Bridge Captain textures were hand-painted in Photoshop. I used the modeling tools to keep geometry intentionally simple, then relied on stylized textures, lighting, silhouettes, and color separation to give the environment and characters enough visual identity without requiring high geometric detail.

sections.title: Technical Art Mindset
paragraphs: My focus was always on making the art serve the game rather than treating modeling as a standalone discipline. I approached assets from the perspective of a developer who needed them to fit memory, rendering, gameplay, platform, and performance constraints.

I have also used LOD and model-optimization techniques on other projects, although Bridge Captain VR did not require an additional heavy optimization pass because the assets had already been authored at a deliberately low geometric cost.

sections.title: Later Asset Strategy
paragraphs: As my Unity work expanded, I increasingly relied on purchased production asset libraries when they made more sense than creating everything myself. That allowed me to spend more time on engine, gameplay, systems, and tools while still retaining enough 3D knowledge to modify, integrate, optimize, and direct game assets when needed.
